business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113 (as amended): ss. 4-8 (formation, Memorandum and Articles of Association), s. 24 (registered office), Part IV (directors) and applicable registration provisions; supplementary Tax identification and VAT registration under Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 and VAT Law 95(I)/2000.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 (Application for Incorporation) filed together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association; formal registration evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation and publication in the Official Gazette.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for private limited companies under the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113). The subscribers freely set the authorized share capital; a standard fast-fashion retail distributor typically registers EUR 1,000 (nominal) with initial paid-up of EUR 100-500. No escrow account or capital verification is required for non-regulated e-commerce activity; escrow rules apply only to CySEC-licensed, banking, or other regulated sectors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Company has been incorporated under the Companies Law (Cap. 113) of Cyprus; IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: (1) the Memorandum and Articles of Association, as filed, are ratified; (2) the allotment of subscribed shares to the founding shareholders is approved; (3) the registered office is fixed at [Address], Nicosia, Cyprus; (4) [Director Name] is appointed Director, [Secretary Name] Secretary, and [Representative Name] Tax Representative; (5) the appointed officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute payment-rail agreements, and file all statutory registrations; (6) this resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver - Company Name Reservation Unit, Nicosia (counter and online pre-registration portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Cyprus-licensed advocate submits a name reservation request identifying the proposed entity name, corporate objects, and desired economic activity. The Registrar verifies the proposed name against the company index and registered trademarks, then issues an official Certificate of Name Approval (valid for 12 months) confirming no conflicting or prohibited words.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to three alternative names
Summary of corporate objects (online retail of apparel and footwear, ISIC 4791)
Name search report prepared by the licensed advocate
Passport copies of the founding shareholders
Signed advocate engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identity or similarity with an existing registration, immediately refile using one of the alternative names; alternatively, submit an appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the refusal, supported by a distinctiveness argument and trademark search report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Stamp Duty Assessment and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cyprus-licensed advocate / notary public; the stamped documents are subsequently submitted to the Registrar of Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The advocate drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Greek or English, incorporating objects covering e-commerce retail of fast-fashion apparel and footwear, import/export, fulfillment distribution, digital marketing, and general ancillary powers. Subscribers execute the documents before the advocate, who certifies signatures. The constitution is then submitted to the District Stamp Duty Office for assessment; stamp duty of 0.6% on the authorized share capital is paid and the documents are officially stamped.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of Name Approval
Passport copies and proof of residential address of each subscriber and the first director
Statement of authorized share capital (default EUR 1,000)
Signed consent to act as director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or stamp office queries the objects clause or capital statement, execute an addendum or supplementary declaration before notarization; if stamp duty is under-assessed, pay the differential amount with accrued interest and obtain the revised stamp certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Nicosia (official counter or registered e-filing portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The advocate lodges Form HE1 together with the stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents of officers, and proof of payment of the registration fee. The Registrar examines the filing, registers the legal person in the HE77 series, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, assigns the company registration number, and transmits the incorporation notice for publication in the Official Gazette.
required_dossiers: Form HE1 (Application for Incorporation)
Stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of Name Approval
Consents of the first director and secretary
Power of attorney if the incorporation is executed through an attorney
Official receipt of registration fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a technical query (e.g., incomplete address, capital discrepancy, or missing consent), submit the outstanding document through the same filing channel and pay the administrative resubmission fee; if registration is refused, correct the defect and refile, or appeal to the court under Cap. 113.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification, VAT and EU OSS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus - TAXISnet portal and the competent District Tax Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, apply electronically for the Tax Identification Code (TIC). Register for VAT on TAXISnet because pan-EU B2C distance sales of fast-fashion apparel will exceed the statutory registration threshold (EUR 15,600); simultaneously register for the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme to simplify EU-wide VAT declarations on distance sales. Submit the projected revenue statement, business model description, and banking details.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified registered office address confirmation
Passport copies and TIC declarations of directors and shareholders
Projected turnover statement and e-commerce activity description
Confirmed corporate bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Department submits a clarification query, respond within the statutory deadline through TAXISnet with supplementary evidence; if late VAT registration is identified, cooperate via voluntary disclosure to the Tax Commissioner to regularize the effective date and mitigate penalty exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Social Insurance Services (Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance) and the competent District Labour Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Social Insurance Services to obtain the employer contribution code and payroll withholding account. Notify the District Labour Office of the registered workplace conditions and confirm compliance with working time, health and safety, and maternity/paternity rules for any staff engaged in e-commerce operations, including future warehouse employees.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles
Registered office and workplace address details
Identification documents of the directors
Applicable employer registration forms on the Social Insurance portal
Draft employment contract templates and payroll policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Social Insurance records conflict with Tax Department data, file a harmonization declaration with both authorities; if the employer registration is made late relative to the first hire, regularize through the Social Insurance amnesty procedure and pay any assessed contributions with interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office, Statutory Registers and Appointment of Independent Auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office premises (approved by the board); first board meeting held under the pro-forma resolution; filings with the Registrar of Companies and the competent audit regulator.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the first board meeting, the board adopts the registered office address, approves the statutory registers (shareholders, directors, charges), authorizes the company seal or electronic signature arrangement, and appoints an independent Cyprus-licensed statutory auditor for the inaugural financial year as required by the Companies Law. The registered office consent letter is filed with the Registrar and the auditor's consent is retained in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease agreement or registered office consent letter from the property owner
Pro-forma first board resolution
Consent letter of the independent statutory auditor
Statutory register templates
Company seal or e-signature certificate authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office consent is deficient, replace the premises and file a notice of change of registered office with the Registrar; if the auditor's consent fails, obtain a replacement engagement letter and have the board ratify the substitute appointment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry; Consumer Protection Service; and the District Municipality of the registered operation for any physical fulfillment warehouse.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory sectoral license applies to pure e-commerce retail of fast-fashion apparel. Conditional Municipal Operating Permit for Commercial Warehouse (fulfillment) and, where applicable, product conformity registration under EU General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (with District Administration Office screening coordination).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/Registration category: apparel e-commerce offices and light logistics facilities are not listed in Annexes I-III of the Cyprus EIA Law 127(I)/2018. A discretionary exemption or registration confirmation may be issued where a dedicated fulfillment warehouse exceeds 2,000 m2 or is located in a sensitive urban zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Urban Waste-Water Treatment Directive 91/271/EEC for sanitary effluent discharge; Packaging and Packaging Waste Directive 94/62/EC and Cyprus implementing regulations for packaging take-back quotas; EU Regulation (EU) 2023/988 for consumer product safety and traceability; no material VOC point-source emissions because fast-fashion warehousing and retail do not meet the Industrial Emissions Directive (2010/75/EU) thresholds; compliance with textile waste and extended producer responsibility obligations under EU waste policy is recommended.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the District Fire Service of the Cyprus Fire Service / Civil Defence for occupied premises exceeding 500 m2 or containing storage areas; structural load inspection certificate prepared by a civil engineer and filed with the District Town Planning Office; workplace occupational safety clearance from the Department of Labour Inspection covering ventilation, emergency exits, racking stability, and ergonomic conditions for fulfillment operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of Cyprus, Ministry of Finance; online portal: Taxisnet (https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy); customs matters administered by the Department of Customs and Excise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Private Limited Company with the Registrar of Companies to obtain the HE registration number. 2) The company is automatically registered for income tax with the Tax Department; a Tax Identification Number (TIN) is allocated upon incorporation notification. 3) For VAT, file Form VAT-101 with the Tax Department, attaching the certificate of incorporation, certified memorandum and articles of association, registered office certificate, director and secretary details, and evidence of business premises; for non-EU-established persons, a local tax representative is mandatory. 4) The VAT number is issued in the format CY+8 digits+1 check letter, generally within 30 days. 5) If engaged in intra-EU distance sales or B2C digital services, also register for the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) via Taxisnet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: Cyprus tax-resident companies are taxed on worldwide income at a 12.5% corporate rate with a foreign tax credit; non-resident companies are taxed only on Cyprus-source income. A Cyprus Ltd is not eligible for pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election; Cyprus implements ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules under Law 37(I)/2019. Available elections include: board-management tax-residence determination, Notional Interest Deduction on new equity, IP-Box regime producing a 2.5% effective rate on qualifying intangibles, tonnage tax for shipping, and OSS / IOSS registration elections for cross-border e-commerce. No VAT group registration exists in Cyprus.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Law No. 94(I)/2000, as amended, administered by the Tax Department of Cyprus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover for Cyprus-established taxable persons; no threshold for non-established foreign suppliers, who must register from the first euro of taxable supply; EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold applies for intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C digital services when using the OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance regime as of 2025. E-invoicing is voluntary; B2G invoices to public-sector buyers must be deliverable in the European Standard EN 16931 on request. VAT reporting is via periodic Taxisnet returns and VIES recapitulative statements. Cyprus is preparing for the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposal; real-time digital reporting and mandatory e-invoicing are expected to be phased in from 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (1) exports of goods to non-EU destinations under section 55 of the VAT Law, subject to proof that goods left the EU within 90 days of supply; (2) intra-Community supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number, reported in the VIES statement under section 59; (3) supplies of ancillary services directly linked to exports. B2C distance sales of fast-fashion goods to EU consumers are not zero-rated and must be taxed at destination via OSS. Domestic B2C retail sales remain subject to 19% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / summary declaration) filed via Cyprus Customs ECS
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR evidencing physical movement out of the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence of export payment, where applicable
Commercial Invoice containing Incoterms, full description, quantity and value of goods
Customer's VAT registration number and contemporaneous VIES validation report for intra-Community supplies
Proof of delivery signed by the customer or carrier tracking document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Tax Department may raise VAT assessments within 6 years of the tax period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or wilful neglect. False export zero-rating claims attract a 10% late-payment penalty on the unpaid VAT plus an additional 1% per month for continuing default, default interest, and retrospective clawback of any refunds paid. Fraudulent evasion can lead to civil penalties up to 100% of the tax evaded and criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 5 years. Customs enforcement measures include seizure of goods, asset distraint and Winding-up proceedings. Note: Cyprus itself imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day reference reflects the ultimate beneficial owner's home-country exchange-control obligations, non-compliance with which may trigger reversal of export refunds in the source jurisdiction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus is a Eurozone member using the Euro (EUR) with full capital and current account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There is no Cypriot exchange-control law, no Central Bank of Cyprus prior-approval requirement for equity injection, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or trade settlement, and no restriction on holding foreign currency. The only regulatory layers are: (i) balance-of-payments statistical reporting under Regulation (EC) No 1849/2005, administered by the Central Bank of Cyprus for individual cross-border transactions at or above the prescribed threshold; and (ii) AML and travel-rule verification under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113. Profit and dividend remittance requires a valid shareholder resolution, sufficient distributable reserves under the Cyprus Companies Law, and up-to-date tax filings, but does not require any FX authorization or conversion license.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Cyprus. Export receipts from the fast-fashion e-commerce business may be freely retained in the original currency (USD, GBP, etc.), freely converted into EUR, or used offshore. The Central Bank of Cyprus merely imposes balance-of-payments statistical reporting on banks for transactions above the reporting threshold; there is no repatriation deadline and no mandatory exchange of export proceeds into EUR.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a complementary treasury and cross-border payout rail, but Low as a sole settlement infrastructure. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions, including those passporting into Cyprus under PSD2 and the EMD2 regime, may aggregate e-commerce proceeds and provide SWIFT-comparable disbursement rails. However, an EMI cannot maintain a capital escrow account or take deposits, must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts at a Tier-1 credit institution, and requires a sponsoring correspondent bank. For the target rails (Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments), an EMI overlay is viable only where the merchant acquirer holds an EU banking or payment-institution license; routing PSP waterfalls directly into an omnibus EMI account creates AML mixing flags and may trigger payment-institution licensing issues under the Central Bank of Cyprus.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners, Tier-1 Cypriot banks uniformly mandate at least one physical appearance during initial onboarding. A fully remote opening is permitted only for low-risk profiles using eIDAS-certified electronic identity verification recognized under the Central Bank of Cyprus KYC Directive; in practice, the principal UBO and at least one authorized signatory should attend an in-person interview at the bank's Nicosia branch. Thereafter, periodic in-person or video-facilitated compliance reviews are scheduled every 12 to 24 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce settlement arriving from third-party payment service providers (Klarna and Shopify Payments) with mixed chargebacks, refunds, and BNPL receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant services agreements; PSP settlement statements and payout timelines; platform order-level reconciliation exports (orders, payments, refunds); VIES VAT registration and Cyprus TAX ID certificate; chargeback and BNPL provisioning policies; and a Board-approved cash-flow model presented to the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply-chain nexus with Chinese fast-fashion manufacturers creating perceived exposure to high-risk jurisdictions and third-party factoring arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proforma invoices and purchase orders; customs declarations and bills of lading; underlying trade contracts with arm's-length pricing; bank reference letters from Chinese counterparty banks; OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation demonstrating gross-margin adequacy; and a copy of the freight-forwarder and factoring agreement if any financing structure is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex UBO chain, nominee shareholding, or multiple holding-company layers obscuring source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate register chain with apostilled certificates of incorporation and registered office; statutory UBO declaration forms under the Cyprus AML Directive; source-of-wealth statement with supporting asset or liquidation evidence; Cyprus economic substance dossier including lease agreement, local employment contracts, Board minutes, and audited financial statements; and confirmation that no beneficial owner appears on national, EU, or UN sanctions or PEP lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 with the ECB balance-of-payments purpose code for 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' and ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPI' (Capital Payments), executed over TARGET2 for EUR or CHIPS/Fedwire for USD. The accompanying documentation bundle includes the notarized shareholder and board allotment resolutions, share premium ledger entry, issued share certificates, and the bank's KYC forms. The receiving bank is obligated to transmit transaction details to the Central Bank of Cyprus balance-of-payments statistical system where the amount exceeds the reporting threshold. Travel-rule compliance under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 requires complete originator and beneficiary information in MT103 fields 50 and 59. No FX conversion or Central Bank approval is required for the capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and intercompany disbursements; SWIFT MT700 Commercial Letters of Credit for documented fast-fashion purchase orders above EUR 100,000; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EU suppliers; and cross-currency settlement to Chinese manufacturers via EUR/USD or EUR/CNY NDF-funded disbursements using Tier-1 correspondent banks. Reconciliation is performed through SWIFT FIN field 72 narration and ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 messages. Net settlements from Shopify Payments and Klarna BNPL are routed to the operational EUR account through the acquiring bank's daily clearing file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts with tenors from 1 to 24 months under ISDA 1992 or 2002 CSA with EU-authorized bank counterparties

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EUR/CNY and USD/CNY executed through the London desks of EU-authorized dealers to hedge Chinese supplier exposure; NDFs require client classification as professional or eligible counterparty under MiFID II
Cross-currency swaps on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH for balance-sheet hedging of working-capital, intercompany receivables, and future purchase-order commitments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form HE32) together with Financial Statements (for non-audit-exempt companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Energy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 75 for the first month plus EUR 25 per month thereafter (maximum EUR 250); prolonged default may trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Levy payment under the Companies (Annual Levy) Law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June each year (new companies incorporated after 30 June pay the first levy by 30 June of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of EUR 25 plus interest at 5% per annum; persistent non-payment may lead to strike-off and legal recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the tax year (e.g., for tax year 2024, due by 31 December 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 50 per month or part thereof (maximum EUR 500); interest at 5% per annum on outstanding tax and potential director personal liability for persistent default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required unless the company qualifies as a 'small company' under Section 66A of the Companies Law, Cap. 113, by satisfying at least two of three criteria for two consecutive financial years: (i) average number of employees not exceeding 10; (ii) balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 350,000; (iii) net turnover not exceeding EUR 700,000. Non-exempt companies must appoint a certified auditor and file audited financial statements with the Registrar.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the European Union; small eligible companies may apply IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cyprus law does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. The Annual Return (Form HE32) functions as the annual statutory confirmation of the shareholder/member register, thereby implicitly confirming UBO data. Any shareholding transfer or other change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the Central Beneficial Ownership Register within 30 days, with simultaneous updating of the company's internal UBO register and statutory books.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (resolutions of members and directors)
Register of Charges (mortgages and charges over assets)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $324 – $1,080 per year (typical service provider range for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,620 – $5,400 per year (typical certified audit fee for a small e-commerce retail company)
